props.title: Mixed Nuts

sections.content: **Mixed Nuts** (1994) represents Nora Ephron's oddball attempt at dark holiday comedy, starring Steve Martin as the head of a suicide prevention hotline on Christmas Eve. While it stumbled at release, it's gained cult status alongside other unconventional Christmas films like **The Ref** (1994) and **Scrooged** (1988). The film's ensemble cast including Madeline Kahn, Rita Wilson, and Adam Sandler in an early role creates a chaotic energy that mirrors its Los Angeles setting during the holidays.

sections.content: Mixed Nuts follows a tradition of Christmas films that subvert holiday expectations, like **Bad Santa** (2003) and **Go** (1999). Its Venice Beach setting provides a sunny contrast to traditional snowy Christmas movies, similar to **L.A. Story** (1991) and **Kiss Kiss Bang Bang** (2005). The film's mix of dark themes with slapstick comedy echoes earlier ensemble holiday pieces like **200 Cigarettes** (1999).

Nora Ephron's direction here markedly differs from her more successful romantic comedies like **Sleepless in Seattle** (1993) and **You've Got Mail** (1998). The film's tonal shifts between suicidal callers and physical comedy represent a challenging balance that later holiday dark comedies like **The Ice Harvest** (2005) would attempt to perfect. sections.content: Mixed Nuts arrived during a surge of alternative Christmas films in the 1990s, including **Die Hard** (1988) and **Gremlins** (1984) as early influences. This trend continued with films like **The Long Kiss Goodnight** (1996) and **Reindeer Games** (2000), which used the holiday setting as ironic contrast to their darker themes.
